Merge tag 'char-misc-7.4-rc1' of git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/gregkh/char-misc

Pull Char/Misc/IIO/others driver updates from Greg KH:
 "Here is the big set of char/misc/android/iio and other small driver
  subsystem patches for 7.4-rc1. Loads of stuff in here, larger than
  normal. Highlights include:

   - removal of the C binder code, the rust version is stable and will
     be used going forward in a few billion devices. Great job by those
     developers

   - loads and loads of IIO driver updates and feature additions

   - speakup driver fixes and updates

   - mhi driver updates

   - mei driver updates

   - xillybus driver fixes

   - comedi driver fixes

   - lots of coresight driver updates

   - Interconnect driver updates

   - nvmem driver updates and fixes

   - slimbus driver updates and fixes

   - spmi driver updates and fixes

   - lots of tiny misc and char driver fixes based on people scanning
     for things

  All of these have been in linux-next for a while with no reported
  issues, other than a merge conflict with one of the rust tree files,
  which should be simple to resolve"

Merge tag 'for-7.4/block-20261021' of git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/axboe/linux

Pull block updates from Jens Axboe:

 - NVMe updates via Keith:
     - Apple M4 (t8132) ANS2 NVMe support
     - nvme-multipath sysfs attributes for path_state, iopolicies, and
       fail_on_ctrl_loss, plus path state evaluation fixes
     - nvme-tcp parallelized I/O queue allocation and startup, and using
       the caller's network namespace
     - nvmet passthru UAF fix and rework, PR preempt use-after-free
       fixes, auth hardening, and traffic based keep alive support
     - DH-HMAC-CHAP secret attributes readable by root only
     - Various other fixes and cleanups

 - swim driver overhaul and fixes, plus floppy fixes, via a pull from
   Denis

 - Block device buffered and direct I/O rework from Tal: use
   iomap_dirty_folio, take i_rwsem for the write fallback and splice
   read, honor IOCB_NOWAIT in the buffered read path, and reject atomic
   write fallback to buffered I/O

 - Large zone revalidation rework: serialize revalidation, handle
   capacity changes by dropping and retrying zone write plugs, propagate
   read-only and offline conditions, and treat offline and read-only
   zones as dead

 - ublk robustness work around canceled FETCH rounds and going live over
   canceled io commands, dropping the default I/O scheduler, and a batch
   of selftest additions

 - blk-iocost flush cost support and zone append accounting

 - rust block fixes for Send/Sync bounds on GenDisk and TagSet, and
   import style cleanups

 - Atomic write fixes capping size by the PI buffer constraints and
   failing short atomic pins

 - Skip the redundant flush for O_DSYNC direct writes, and only use
   REQ_FUA when the device supports it

 - Store GPT attributes as a raw value

 - Remove support for swapping loop fds

 - Various other fixes and cleanups all over

Pull module updates from Petr Pavlu:

 - Ignore local labels and mapping symbols during module load

   These symbols were already ignored during kallsyms address-to-symbol
   lookups. Filter them out earlier during module loading to reduce
   lookup overhead and prevent them from appearing in /proc/kallsyms.

 - Fix potentially incorrect access of SetOnce<T> when setting Rust
   module parameters.

 - Fix a potential read of an uninitialized count when printing taint
   information for unloaded modules.

 - Allocate the kmod argument array using kmalloc_array() in preparation
   for conversion to type-aware allocators.

 - Clean up includes in linux/kmod.h

   Add explicit includes of linux/umh.h to files that use usermode
   helpers. Then clean up the #include list in linux/kmod.h, notably
   removing the compatibility linux/umh.h include.

 - Remove the error-injection.h include from linux/module.h

   Add explicit includes of linux/error-injection.h to files that use
   the ALLOW_ERROR_INJECTION() macro and currently rely on it being
   provided indirectly via linux/module.h. Then remove the unnecessary
   linux/error-injection.h include from linux/module.h.

 - Replace __MODULE_STRING() with __stringify() in various drivers in
   preparation for removing the former macro.

Merge tag 'mm-stable-2026-10-19-21-33' of git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/akpm/mm

Pull MM updates from Andrew Morton:

 - "selftests/mm: improve khugepaged coverage" (Kiryl Shutsemau):

   Give khugepaged a proper workout. Extend the tests to all supported
   mTHP orders, check exactly which windows collapsed, and make scan
   completion deterministic. Race collapse against faults, pinning, fork
   and remap; verify that the contents survive.

   Add coverage for whole-page-table zaps and memory pressure too.

 - "selftests/mm: separate GUP microbenchmarking from functional testing"
   (Sarthak Sharma):

   Untangle GUP benchmarking from correctness testing. Move the
   benchmark into tools/mm, add a standalone harness-based GUP selftest,
   and move shared helpers into tools/lib/mm. Give each tool one job
   instead of mixing timing measurements with correctness checks.

   Cover the mapping, pinning and batch-size combinations explicitly.

 - "mm: Switch device DAX to section-based vmemmap optimization" (Muchun
   Song):

   Apply section-based vmemmap optimization to device DAX. Rework the
   backing metadata layout to save memory while preserving the handling
   of device memory hotplug and its different alignment and lifetime
   requirements.

 - "mm: Introduce section-based vmemmap optimization for HugeTLB"
   (Muchun Song):

   Cut the memory consumed by HugeTLB's struct page array with
   section-based vmemmap optimization. Arrange the metadata so large
   huge pages need fewer backing pages, while keeping initialization,
   teardown and the various hugepage configurations straight.

 - "mm/huge_memory: clean up and decouple the anon and file split
   helpers" (Kairui Song):

   Separate anonymous and file-backed folio splitting, which have rather
   different locking and bookkeeping requirements. Move the work into
   separate helpers, drop dead checks and tidy swap-cache handling. Fix
   error paths, including one that could leave a folio frozen.

   Keep the swap cache cases separate from file-cache splitting.

 - "mm: Unconditional per-VMA locks and cleanups" (Dave Hansen):

   Make per-VMA locking unconditional and clean up the old conditional
   code around it. This removes configuration-dependent plumbing and
   lets callers depend on one locking model rather than carrying both
   cases along.

 - "memcg: remove the v1 soft limit" (Shakeel Butt):

   Remove the old cgroup v1 memory soft-limit machinery. This has long
   since been superseded by the newer memory-control interfaces; hauling
   around a separate reclaim scheme for it no longer buys us much.

 - "read proc/pid/smaps_rollup under per-vma lock" (Suren Baghdasaryan):

   Read /proc/PID/smaps_rollup using per-VMA locks where possible,
   rather than holding mmap_lock across the entire walk. Retain the
   contention fallback and add tearing tests. This considerably reduces
   latency when another thread is busy changing its mappings.

 - "mm/damon: introduce data access-as-a-data attribute" (SJ Park):

   Teach DAMON to expose memory access observations as data attributes,
   making them available to the probe and filtering machinery. Extend
   the interfaces, documentation and tests so the new information can be
   used rather than merely collected.

 - "Remove PG_private by using page/folio->private checks instead" (Zi
   Yan):

   Get rid of PG_private and use the folio's private pointer to say
   whether private data is attached. Convert the filesystem users,
   including erofs, f2fs and md, and clean up the old accessors and
   flags. There are a few special cases, notably swapcache and hugetlb,
   which need explicit care.

 - "mm: make userland page table freeing RCU-safe" (Lorenzo Stoakes):

   Make freeing userspace page tables safe against RCU readers. Sort out
   the page-table lifetime and locking rules so walkers cannot stumble
   over freed tables while mappings are being torn down.

 - "make unused huge shrinker memcg aware" (Qi Zheng):

   Make shmem's unused-huge-folio shrinker aware of memory cgroups, so
   reclaim can find those folios under the right memcg. Wire up the
   per-memcg tracking and its lifetime rules, and give the shrinklist
   its own lockdep class to avoid spurious dependency reports.

 - "mm: Drop pxd_ERROR()" (Anshuman Khandual):

   Remove the old pxd_ERROR() page-table checks and their
   architecture-specific baggage. Simplify the common page-table
   interfaces and callers now that these checks no longer serve a
   useful purpose.

 - "memcg: group struct fields by access pattern" (Shakeel Butt):

   Rearrange memcg's hot and cold fields according to how they're
   actually accessed. Keep frequently updated counters and their
   neighboring state from fighting over cachelines and reduce needless
   cacheline traffic.

 - "mm/damon/core: fix the size charged for a filter-trimmed region"
   (Donggeun Yoo):

   Fix DAMOS quota accounting when a filter trims a monitoring region.
   Charge only the part left after filtering, not the original region,
   and add KUnit coverage. Previously the excluded memory could eat into
   the quota and make schemes run more slowly than requested.

 - "mm/damon: add kunit and selftests for probes and probe weights" (SJ
   Park):

   Add more tests for DAMON probes and their weights, including
   validation and the results reported to userspace. This is mostly
   about catching regressions in the newer probe infrastructure before
   they become harder to diagnose.

 - "mm: memcontrol: constify the read side of the read side of the memcg
   API" (Tal Zussman):

   Mark the read-only parts of the memcg interface const, from folio and
   lruvec accessors to counters and swap helpers. Most of this is
   mechanical, but it makes the contracts clearer and lets the compiler
   catch accidental writes.

 - "mm/damon/vaddr: support {prep,apply}_probes" (SJ Park):

   Support the new prepare/apply probe operations in DAMON's
   virtual-address backend. This brings vaddr monitoring into line with
   the probe infrastructure and makes the added probe types useful there
   too.

 - "mm/mglru: clean up folio counters and flag usage" (Kairui Song):

   Simplify MGLRU's folio counters and flag handling. Remove redundant
   accounting paths and make the state transitions easier to follow
   without changing the intended reclaim policy.

 - "arch, mm/execmem: resolve confusion about set_direct_map_valid_noflush()"
   (Mike Rapoport (Microsoft)):

   Clarify and straighten out the set_direct_map_valid_noflush()
   interface across architectures and execmem. Make the requested
   mapping changes and the callers' expectations agree, rather than
   relying on subtly different architecture behavior.

 - "mm: zswap: free cold writeback folios promptly" (Alexandre Ghiti):

   Free zswap writeback folios as soon as their disk write completes.
   They are cold temporary buffers, so putting them on the LRU only
   makes reclaim rediscover them later. Extend swap-cache dropbehind and
   let zswap keep these folios off the LRU altogether.

 - "mm: gup: cleanup gup_fast call chain" (Aristeu Rozanski):

   Clean up the GUP-fast call chain and simplify how the fast-path
   helpers pass their arguments and results around. Keep the page-pin
   behavior the same while making the call sequence easier to maintain.

 - "mm: optimize zone-device memmap initialization" (Li Zhe):

   Speed up initialization of zone-device struct pages. Avoid redundant
   work when setting up large device-memory ranges, where touching every
   descriptor can get expensive.

 - "mm/zswap: shrink zswap_entry via a pool id" (Jianyue Wu):

   Reduce the size of zswap_entry by storing a compact pool identifier
   instead of a full pointer. Keep the pool lookup and lifetime handling
   correct while saving per-entry metadata.

 - "mm/damon: support access monitoring of hugetlb-backed memory"
   (Krishna Iyer):

   Let DAMON monitor hugetlb-backed memory too. Extend the relevant
   access checks and add coverage so those mappings no longer fall
   through a hole in the monitoring machinery.

 - "mm/execmem: fixes and cleanups for the ROX cache" (Mike Rapoport):

   Tidy execmem's read-only-executable cache and fix its handling of the
   awkward allocation and release cases. The aim is to make the cache's
   ownership and permission transitions more predictable.

 - "zsmallc: remove old object read API" (Sergey Senozhatsky):

   Drop zsmalloc's old object-read API and move its remaining users to
   the supported access mechanism. This removes a duplicate interface
   which we no longer need.

 - "mm/mempolicy: stop copying state in the interleave paths" (Gregory
   Price):

   Stop copying mempolicy state in the interleave paths when a reference
   to the existing policy will do. This avoids extra work and makes the
   ownership rules less obscure.

 - "mm/mglru: speed up inc_min_seq() and fix cold/hot inversions" (Barry
   Song):

   Make MGLRU's generation advancement cheaper and fix cases where cold
   and hot folios end up in the wrong order. Adjust the counter and list
   handling so reclaim doesn't keep passing over the better eviction
   candidates.

 - "mm: Fix MF_DELAYED handling on memory failure" (Lisa Wang):

   Treat MF_DELAYED as a partially completed memory-failure operation,
   not an outright failure. Propagate that result correctly through
   shmem and the generic handler, fix the extra-reference accounting,
   and add tests for the resulting SIGBUS behavior.

 - "tools/mm/page_owner_sort: fix --sort, add module filter, improve
   usage" (Ye Liu):

   Fix page_owner_sort's --sort handling, add module-based filtering and
   make the usage output more helpful. This makes the tool less
   frustrating when tracking down who is holding on to pages.

 - "mm/damon: move damos filter range arguments validation to core" (SJ
   Park):

   Move DAMOS filter range validation into the core, where all callers
   can share it. Also close the sysfs read-twice races which could pass
   inconsistent ranges, and add tests for invalid input.

 - "mm/damon: misc cleanups" (Zenghui Yu):

   Clean up a collection of small DAMON rough edges in the core,
   interfaces and tests. No large behavior change here, just simpler
   code and fewer opportunities for confusion.

 - "mm/damon: cleanup code, add test cases, and update guidances in
   docs" (SJ Park):

   Clean up DAMON's core and interfaces, add missing test cases and
   bring the documentation into line with the code. These changes should
   make the newer facilities easier to understand and maintain.

 - "mm/damon: introduce hugepage_size probe filter" (SJ Park):

   Add a DAMON probe filter for hugepage size. Let users select a range
   of folio sizes through sysfs, validate the range and document the new
   interface, so monitoring can concentrate on memory backed by the
   desired hugepage sizes.

 - "selftests/mm: pagemap_ioctl test fixes and cleanups" (Zenghui Yu):

   Fix some pagemap ioctl test assumptions and clean up their setup and
   reporting. Make failures point to the operation that went wrong
   rather than to test harness bookkeeping.

 - "mm: avoid large folio splits when swap is unavailable" (Johannes
   Weiner):

   Avoid splitting large folios merely to attempt swap when no swap
   space is available. There is little point paying for an expensive
   split when reclaim cannot actually swap the resulting pages out.

 - "mm: workingset: fix the shadow node budget under MGLRU" (Hui Zhu):

   Fix the workingset shadow-node budget with MGLRU enabled. Keep the
   shadow entries within the intended limits so refault tracking does
   not quietly consume more metadata than it should.

 - "selftests/mm: TAP output and global-state fixes" (Song Hu):

   Fix selftests which produce misleading TAP output or fail to restore
   global settings after a run. A test ought to leave the system as it
   found it, particularly when a whole suite follows behind.

 - "mm: remove page_swap_entry()" (Tal Zussman):

   Remove page_swap_entry() and convert its remaining users to the folio
   and swap-entry helpers. Lose an old page-level interface and make the
   swap paths a little more consistent.

 - "mm: refactor zonelist constructors and iterators" (Gregory Price):

   Refactor the zonelist construction and walk helpers to reduce
   duplicated logic. Keep the allocation ordering rules intact while
   making it clearer how zones are selected.

 - "mm: kmemleak: batch the struct page scan" (Breno Leitao):

   Scan adjacent struct pages in batches instead of taking kmemleak_lock
   once for every single page. This preserves scan coverage and the
   lock-hold bound, while cutting overhead substantially on debug
   kernels.

 - "mm/damon: misc improvements in tests and documents" (Zenghui Yu):

   Fix some DAMON selftests which leave kdamond running or fail under
   Python safe-path mode, and improve the KUnit coverage and
   documentation. Nothing especially glamorous, but these are worth
   doing.

 - "mm/damon: introduce probe_hits_wsum DAMOS core filter" (SJ Park):

   Add a DAMOS core filter using weighted probe-hit counts. This gives
   schemes another way to select regions based on what the monitoring
   probes observed.

 - "mm/mglru: fix ineffective memory protection for non-kswapd reclaim"
   (Ridong Chen):

   Fix MGLRU's memory protection handling for reclaim outside kswapd.
   The protection settings weren't having the intended effect in these
   paths, leaving protected memory more exposed than requested.

 - "mm/damon: improve readability, clarity and test coverage" (SJ Park):

   Simplify a handful of DAMON core helpers, clarify their behavior and
   expand test coverage. There are no intended userspace-visible changes
   in this batch.

 - "mm: replace PF_KCOMPACTD/PF_KSWAPD with kthread_func()" (Kefeng
   Wang):

   Stop identifying reclaim and compaction workers through the PF_KSWAPD
   and PF_KCOMPACTD task flags. Use their kthread functions instead and
   remove the redundant flag plumbing.

 - "mm/hugetlb: fix surplus accounting and availability checks during
   demotion" (Longlong Xia):

   Fix HugeTLB surplus accounting and availability checks when demoting
   huge pages. Keep the counters and reservation decisions consistent as
   one huge page turns into several smaller ones.

 - "mm/damon: add kunit tests for probe_hits handling and probe params
   validation" (Jason Angelov):

   Add KUnit tests for DAMON probe-hit handling and invalid probe
   parameters. These cover edge cases that were too easy to miss in
   ordinary monitoring tests.

 - "mm/damon: fix misc bugs in kunit, quota goals and sysfs refresh_ms"
   (SJ Park):

   Fix a few DAMON bugs in KUnit tests, quota-goal handling and the
   sysfs refresh interval. Small fixes, but the incorrect results and
   control behavior were real.

 - "mm: zswap: optimize zswap invalidate and store" (Kefeng Wang):

   Simplify zswap's invalidate and store paths to avoid avoidable
   lookups and work. Keep the entry lifetime rules intact while making
   those frequent operations cheaper.

 - "mm: replace custom ratelimiting logic" (Pedro Falcato):

   Replace hand-rolled MM rate limiting with the common kernel helpers.
   There is no need to maintain another local version of the same
   mechanism.

 - "mm/vmalloc: minor cleanups" (Ye Liu):

   Tidy some vmalloc initialization and reporting code, and pull
   duplicated vmap-area insertion work into a helper. No functional
   changes are intended.

 - "mm/mglru: clean up isolate_folios for readability and clarity"
   (Ridong Chen):

   Clean up MGLRU's isolate_folios() so the decisions are easier to read
   and verify. Keep reclaim behavior unchanged while removing
   unnecessary twists in the control flow.

 - "Catch automatic storage in IDA and Maple Tree definitions" (Yury
   Norov):

   Catch IDA and maple-tree definitions placed in automatic storage
   where the lifetime rules are wrong or easy to get wrong. Add checks
   so such mistakes are harder to slip through unnoticed.

 - "mm, swap: some random fixes and cleanups" (Kemeng Shi):

   Fix and simplify a few unrelated swap paths, removing redundant work
   and tidying up error handling. A small collection of things which
   were better fixed than left lying around.

 - "mm/page_io: folio conversion cleanups" (Tal Zussman):

   Finish some page-to-folio conversions in swap I/O, removing obsolete
   wrappers and using folio operations consistently. The I/O behavior is
   intended to remain the same.

 - "mm/swap: skip empty clusters in the swapoff scan" (Youngjun Park):

   Skip empty swap clusters during swapoff instead of walking slots
   which have nothing to release. This avoids pointless work on sparsely
   used swap devices.

 - "mm: trace: decode architecture-specific VMA flags" (Meijing Zhao):

   Teach the VMA trace output to decode architecture-specific flags,
   rather than leaving them as unexplained bits. That should make
   tracing a good deal more useful when debugging unusual mappings.

 - "mm, swap: don't spin on a bad swap entry" (Breno Leitao):

   Stop repeatedly retrying a swap entry which is already known to be
   bad. Make the error path terminate cleanly instead of wasting CPU
   chasing an entry that cannot be used.

 - "mm/page_isolation: fix UBSAN shift-out-of-bounds in
   isolate_single_pageblock" (Qi Xi):

   Fix an out-of-range shift in isolate_single_pageblock() and tighten
   its associated boundary handling. UBSAN found the issue; the result
   should be more robust pageblock isolation.

 - "mm: khugepaged: fix tracepoint UAF" (Vernon Yang):

   Fix a use-after-free in khugepaged tracepoint handling. Make sure the
   information recorded by tracing stays valid for as long as the trace
   event needs it.

 - "mm/damon: fix DAMOS bugs in core, paddr and vaddr" (SJ Park):

   Fix several DAMOS problems across the core and physical- and
   virtual-address backends. The changes close error cases and bring the
   implementations back into agreement.

 - "mm/hugetlb_cgroup: move the per-node usage along with the folio"
   (Hongfu Li):

   Move HugeTLB per-node usage accounting when folios migrate between
   nodes or are reparented to another cgroup. Otherwise numa_stat can
   retain stale charges and even underflow when the folio is freed.

 - "docs/core-api: memory-allocation: add k[mz]alloc_obj() and clarify
   kmalloc" (Mike Rapoport):

   Document the typed k[mz]alloc_obj() allocation helpers and clear up
   some kmalloc guidance. Make it easier for callers to choose the right
   interface.

 - "selftests/mm: Validate selections and scope memfd_secret setup"
   (Tianyi Chen):

   Check selftest selections before running and confine memfd_secret
   setup to the cases that actually need it. Avoid confusing failures
   caused by the test harness itself.

 - "mm/damon: move zero damos quota target_value handling to the core
   layer" (SJ Park):

   Handle a zero DAMOS quota goal target in the core rather than making
   each user of the interface invent its own rule. Keep quota decisions
   consistent across callers.

 - "mm/damon: Introduce a huge page collapsing mechanism using auto
   tuning" (Asier Gutierrez):

   Add an auto-tuned DAMON mechanism for collapsing huge pages. Use
   monitoring feedback to decide when collapse is worthwhile rather than
   forcing one fixed policy onto every workload.

 - "kmemleak: fix stale documentation and raise the verbose default"
   (Breno Leitao):

   Bring the kmemleak documentation up to date and require a third
   confirming scan before verbose kernels print a suspected leak. The
   extra scan helps suppress transient false positives in noisy debug
   builds.

 - "mm/memory: improve insert_pages() error handling" (Avi Weiss):

   Tighten insert_pages() error handling so partial failures are
   reported and cleaned up consistently. The caller should not have to
   guess how far the operation got.

 - "mm/damon: allow NULL or unstarted damon_ctx parameter for
   damon_call()" (SJ Park):

   Make damon_call() handle NULL and not-yet-started contexts safely.
   Simplify the rules for callers and avoid an indefinite wait on an
   invalid state.

 - "mm/damon: introduce pgidle_set probe filter type" (SJ Park):

   Add a pgidle_set DAMON probe filter, giving monitoring users another
   way to select pages by their idle-tracking state. Wire it through the
   filter interfaces and tests.

 - "mm/damon/core: remove unused helper functions" (Cheng-Han Wu):

   Remove DAMON core helpers which no longer have callers. Keep the API
   surface smaller rather than retaining dead code just in case.

 - "mm: stop calling pmd_folio() on special PMDs" (Gregory Price):

   Avoid calling pmd_folio() on special PMD mappings that have no struct
   page. The old assumption could fault in procfs walkers; use the
   normal-folio checks and handle those mappings properly.

 - "mm: remove three unused helpers from mm.h" (Tal Zussman):

   Remove three unused helpers from mm.h. Fewer obsolete interfaces for
   the next person to stumble over.

 - "mm/damon: improvements in efficiency, error handling, documents"
   (Liew Rui Yan):

   Skip needless DAMOS quota work once the quota is full, propagate a
   missing sysfs error and tidy a couple of comments. The ignored error
   could make a monitoring-start request appear successful when it
   wasn't.

 - "docs/mm/damon/design: add explanation of nr_snapshots" (Liew Rui
   Yan):

   Explain DAMON's nr_snapshots accounting in the design documentation
   and straighten out the associated terminology. Make it clearer what
   users should expect from that counter.

 - "selftests/cgroup: fixes for test_zswap on single core VM" (Wilson
   Felipe Pereira):

   Fix two test_zswap failures on single-CPU VMs. Wait for the exiting
   child's cgroup to become unpopulated before reconfiguring it, and
   avoid another test assumption which breaks under constrained
   scheduling.

 - "docs/ksm: fix advisor documentation and comment" (Jinjiang Tu):

   Correct the KSM advisor documentation and a misleading code comment.
   Keep the description aligned with how the advisor actually works.

 - "Fix bugs in HugeTLB allocation when mem_cgroup_charge_hugetlb()
   fails" (Ackerley Tng):

   Fix HugeTLB allocation cleanup when the memcg charge fails. Make sure
   failure exits undo what was allocated rather than leaving stale
   accounting or resources behind.

 - "mm, memcg: fix memory.peak reset clobbering other fds' watermark"
   (Ridong Chen):

   Fix memory.peak reset handling so resetting one file descriptor
   doesn't overwrite the watermark kept for another. Keep those per-open
   measurements independent as intended.

 - "mm: reject zone device folios in more folio walkers" (Gregory
   Price):

   Reject zone-device folios in page walkers that cannot safely handle
   them. Extend the existing checks rather than assuming every folio has
   ordinary system-memory backing.

 - "percpu: remove code with no effect" (Sang-Heon Jeon):

   Remove a few pieces of percpu code which no longer do anything. There
   is no reason to keep maintaining dead paths.

        now configurable per netns (inheritance from init_net is
        controlled by the new net.core.neigh_inherit_init_net sysctl)
      - RCU-protected configuration and rtnl_lock-less fill_info() for
        hsr, netkit, sit, vlan and vxlan devices
      - per-netns device unregistration for ip tunnel and gre devices
      - use the netdev instance lock instead of rtnl_lock when reading
        speed and duplex via sysfs
      - batch the flushing of uncached routes at device unregistration
        time, relieving rtnl_lock contention on netns dismantle.

   - Add hardware pacing offload support, admin-controlled via a new
     rtnetlink attribute, with sch_fq integration (implemented in idpf).

   - Re-segment BIG TCP GSO packets into GSO packets fitting the egress
     device limits instead of plain MSS-sized segments, improving
     throughput for mixed BIG TCP / non-BIG TCP paths by up to 70%.

   - Generate RSS keys that spread flows over all the RX queues; the
     previous random keys could leave some queues unused.

   - Optimize the bridge VLAN forwarding paths: cache the port-VLAN in
     fdb entries and consider only VLAN members when flooding, for ~10%
     more Mpps in the fdb forwarding path.

   - A few TCP/IP performance improvements aimed at efficient cache
     usage and reducing contention.

   - Add the TCP ROCCET congestion control, a CUBIC variant aimed at
     avoiding bufferbloat in cellular networks.

   - Continue the conversion of getsockopt callbacks to sockopt_t.

   - Add an ethtool command to list the front-facing ports of an
     interface, including SFP cages and modules, using the phy_port
     representation.

   - Enable BIG TCP support for bareudp tunnels.

   - Remove the IPV6_ADDRFORM socket option and disallow buggy TCP state

     connect(AF_UNSPEC) + listen()).

   - Remove most BUG_ON()s from core packet processing, replacing them
     with error paths.

  Wireless:

   - Latency improvements, including lockless station get/dump and
     beacon updates, plus RTNL reduction and locking cleanups.

   - Infrastructure for non-station TX/RX with MLO.

   - NAN (Wi-Fi Aware) Instant Communication support and other NAN
     improvements.

   - Control frame Integrity Protocol (CIP) and protected TWT support.

   - Improvements for AP regulatory checks.

  Netfilter:

   - Disable br_netfilter in user namespaces and schedule it for removal
     in 2027.

   - Restrict the raw table in nft_compat to the specific family, hook
     and priority.

     versa).

     integration with memcg.

     dumps, and fix nfnetlink_hook handling of large dumps.

           preparation for netdev support.

      - Meta (fbnic):
         - support large io_uring zero-copy RX buffers
      - Microsoft vNIC (mana):
         - add BQL support

   - Ethernet NICs consumer, and embedded:
      - Airoha:
         - LRO offload support
      - Cadence (macb):
         - context swapping for ringparam and MTU changes, avoiding
           buffer loss under memory pressure
      - Mucse (rnpgbe):
         - TX/RX and link status support
      - NXP (enetc):
         - SR-IOV improvements and VF support for ENETC v4
      - Qualcomm (ppe):
         - IPQ5424 support
      - Realtek PCI (r8169):
         - phylink support
         - RSS support for RTL8127
      - Renesas (ravb):
         - gPTP support for R-Car Gen4
      - Synopsys (stmmac):
         - XDP multi-buffer support on the TX side
         - tc mqprio hw queue priority offload
         - support for RK3568 SGMII, Allwinner H616 EMAC1, UltraRISC
           DP1000 and Qualcomm sa8255p

   - Ethernet switches:
      - Mediatek (mt7530):
         - fast age and change conduit support
      - Microchip (ksz):
         - support for KSZ8995XA/KS8995XA
      - Microchip (lan966x):
         - PCIe FDMA support, ~20x throughput increase in PCIe endpoint
      - Microchip (sparx5):
         - Time Aware Shaper (taprio) offload
      - Motorcomm (yt921x):
         - LED and SerDes PCS support
      - Realtek (rtl8365mb):
         - EEE support

   - Ethernet PHYs:
      - Broadcom:
         - enable jumbo frames on BCM54xx
      - Realtek:
         - support for RTL8261CE_CG and RTL8261D_VM
         - MDIO support for RTL838x and RTL839x

   - WiFi drivers:
      - Broadcom (brcmfmac):
         - FT/OKC roaming offload

         - UHR sniffer support

   - Bluetooth:
      - move H:4 reassembly into the Bluetooth core
      - add generic support for vendor packets
      - MGMT: add security level changed event

   - Bluetooth drivers:

      - Intel: support Draco and Titan Lake, allow unsigned firmware

     error handling in the ACPI CPPC library (Christian Loehle and Sumit
     Gupta)

     cpufreq driver and create the FIE worker before enabling PCC
     callbacks in it to avoid queueing work through a missing worker and
     dereferencing a NULL pointer (Christian Loehle)

   - Update the CPPC cpufreq driver entry in MAINTAINERS and add a new

rust: fwctl: declare cfi_encoding for fwctl_rpc_scope

Currently, VTable::fw_rpc_callback() takes scope as a u32, whereas C
calls fwctl_ops::fw_rpc with enum fwctl_rpc_scope. With kCFI enabled,
enum types are encoded distinctly from integers, causing every fw_rpc
indirect call into a Rust fwctl driver to trip a CFI failure. Thus,
generate fwctl_rpc_scope as a newtype with a cfi_encoding attribute and
use it in fw_rpc_callback().

Pull lsm updates from Paul Moore:

 - Add LSM hooks, object blobs, and audit records for namespaces

   Add the necessary bits to enable LSMs to enforce access controls on
   the management of various kernel namespaces. While this pull request
   does not contain any in-tree users of these hooks, the Landlock pull
   request for Linux v7.4 will include Landlock support and the next
   merge window will likely include SELinux support as well. Considering
   the development behind these hooks, I expect that BPF LSM developers
   will also be making use of the namespace hooks, if they haven't
   already.

 - Update the inode LSM hooks to include mount idmaps

   This allows LSMs to incorporate the mount ID mapping into their
   access control decisions. While there are no current in-tree users of
   this, it was requested by those developing BPF LSM programs and this
   pull request includes a BPF LSM selftest.

 - Preserve the full 32-bit ioctl command in LSM audit records

   Previously only the low 16 bits were logged, ignoring the direction
   and size information in the upper 16 bits. The pull request also
   includes a Landlock based selftest to verify the full 32-bit ioctl
   value.

 - Ensure we don't call security_backing_file_free() multiple times

   Thankfully we don't have a problem with the current code base, but we
   want to fix this behavior now before it becomes a problem.

 - Clarify that only the current task may access current->cred

   The current code is a bit misleading around safely accessing the cred
   field in a task struct. Through comment and code corrections, this
   pull request clarifies that only the task itself may access its cred
   field.

 - Add SLAB_NO_MERGE to the credential object cache

   Harden the credential cache by ensuring credential objects live on
   dedicated slab pages.

 - Make use of safe memory zero'ing in the LSM Rust bindings

 - Update the docs for the current behavior of /sys/kernel/security/lsm

 - Update the docs for CONFIG_LSM and the "lsm=" command line option

 - Remove unnecessary code

rust: module_param: Fix potentially incorrect access of `SetOnce<T>`

The `set_param` function casts `kernel_param.arg` to `*const SetOnce<T>`
But the Rust module macro in rust/macros/module.rs initializes `arg` with
`#param_name.as_void_ptr()`, and `#param_name` is a `ModuleParamAccess<T>`,
not a `SetOnce<T>`.

ModuleParamAccess<T> has default Rust layout but `set_param` accesses its
first field SetOnce<T> assuming it to be at offset 0. This is not
guaranteed by Rust and could cause type confusion leading to data
corruption.

Fix this by casting `kernel_param.arg` to `ModuleParamAccess<T>` and
then accessing the `value: SetOnce<T>` field.

rust: pci: add extended capability and SR-IOV support

Rust PCI drivers have no typed interface for locating and accessing PCIe
extended capabilities.

The SR-IOV extended capability describes VF topology and VF BARs. Expose
this information through the Rust PCI abstraction so drivers can use the
existing typed configuration-space accessors instead of raw bindings.

and add ConfigSpace::find_ext_capability() to locate and project that
layout. Bound the view at the next capability or the end of extended
configuration space. Add ExtSriovRegs and a decoded VF BAR iterator that
reads and validates all six VF BAR register slots up front, yields decoded
BAR addresses and widths in logical order, and keeps the raw
configuration-space slot advancement internal. Since PCI_EXT_CAP_NEXT() is
a function-like macro, expose it through a Rust helper.

Keep raw SR-IOV registers private because PCI core owns their state. Expose
the current First VF Offset through a read-only accessor because the Nova
GSP ABI needs the raw 16-bit First VF Offset in Routing ID space. The
pci_iov_virtfn_devfn() helper instead returns the low eight bits of a
calculated VF Routing ID.

mm: make per-VMA locks available universally

Patch series "mm: Unconditional per-VMA locks and cleanups", v7.

tl;dr: Make per-VMA locks available in all configs.  Simplify some of the
per-VMA lock users now that they can rely on them being always available.

Binder and networking folks: Your code is the target of the cleanups.  I'm
cc'ing you now on v2 because there's emerging consensus on the mm side
that the approach here is sane.  I'm not quite sure how this pile would
get merged, but ack/review tags would be appreciated if this looks good to
you.

Longer version:

When working on some x86 shadow stack code, it was a real pain to avoid
causing recursive locking problems with mmap_lock.  One way to avoid those
was to avoid mmap_lock and use per-VMA locks instead.  They are great, but
they are not available in all configs which makes them unusable in generic
code, or if you want to completely avoid mmap_lock.

Make per-VMA locks available in all configs.  Right now, they are only
available on select architectures when SMP and MMU are enabled.  But all
of the primitives that per-VMA locks are built on (RCU, maple trees,
refcounts) work just fine without SMP or MMU.

The only real downside is that making VMAs a wee bit bigger on !MMU and
!SMP builds.

The upside is much cleaner code, lower complexity and less #ifdeffery.

Clean up a binder VMA locking site now that it can rely on per-VMA locks.

Building on top of universally-available per-VMA locks, introduce a new
helper.  Since the new API does not require callers to have a fallback to
mmap_lock, it's much easier to use.  Callers can potentially replace this
very common kernel idiom:

	mmap_read_lock(mm);
	vma = vma_lookup()
	// fiddle with vma
	mmap_read_unlock(mm);

with:

	vma = vma_start_read_unlocked(mm, address);
	// fiddle with vma
	vma_end_read(vma);

Which avoids mmap_lock entirely in the fast path.

Use that new API for another binder site and one in the TCP code.


This patch (of 7):

The per-VMA locks have been around for several years.  They've had some
bugs worked out of them and have seen quite wide use.  However, they are
still only available when architectures explicitly enable them.  Remove
the conditional compilation around the per-VMA locks, making them
available on all architectures and configs.

The approach up to now seemed to be to add ARCH_SUPPORTS_PER_VMA_LOCK when
the architecture started using per-VMA locks in the fault handler.  But,
contrary to the naming, the Kconfig option does not really indicate
whether the architecture supports per-VMA locks or not.  It is more of a
marker for whether the architecture is likely to benefit from per-VMA
locks.

To me, the most important thing side-effect of universal availability is
letting per-VMA locks be used in SMP=n configs.  This lets us use
per-VMA locking in all x86 code without fallbacks.

Overall, this just generally makes the kernel simpler.  Just look at the
diffstat.  It also opens the door to users that want to use the per-VMA
locks in common code.  Doing *that* brings additional simplifications.

The downside of this is adding some fields to vm_area_struct and
mm_struct.  There are likely ways to optimize this, especially for things
like SMP=n configs.  For now, do the simplest thing: use the same
implementation everywhere.

== Considerations for NOMMU config ==

NOMMU systems do not write-lock VMAs, therefore read-locking a VMA would
always succeed unless VMA is detached.  Therefore for NOMMU config we make
vma_mark_attached() a NOOP, which keeps VMAs always in detached state. 
This causes VMA read-locking to always fail and the caller falls back to
locking mmap_lock.

The following functions will have a different implementation in NOMMU
config:

- vma_mark_attached(), vma_mark_detached() are made NOOPs, keeping VMAs
  always in a detached state and preventing assertions and refcount
  underflows;

- vma_start_write(), vma_start_write_killable() are made NOOPs to avoid
  warnings in __vma_start_write() due to VMAs being detached.  These
  functions are not used in NOMMU code but __vma_start_write() is an
  exported function, therefore might be used by drivers.

- vma_assert_attached() is made NOOP because it's reachable from NOMMU
  code via split_vma()->vma_iter_store_new()->vma_iter_store_overwrite();

- vma_assert_write_locked() is asserting vma->vm_mm is write-locked, as
  was done before this change;

- vma_assert_locked() is asserting vma->vm_mm is locked, as was done
  before this change;

The following functions work for both MMU and NOMMU configs:

- vma_lock_init() performs the same initialization as for MMU config;

- mm_lock_seqcount_init(), mm_lock_seqcount_begin(),
  mm_lock_seqcount_end() are called from mmap_write_{lock|unlock} and
  update mm_lock_seq correctly.

- mmap_lock_speculate_try_begin(), mmap_lock_speculate_retry() work as
  is because mm_lock_seq is updated correctly;

- vma_start_read(), vma_start_read_locked() will always fail because
  VMAs are always detached;

- vma_end_read() will never be called because vma_start_read() never
  succeeds;

- vma_is_attached() always return false because VMAs are always
  detached;

- vma_assert_detached() will never trigger because VMAs are never
  attached;

- vma_start_read_locked() always return false because VMAs are always
  detached;

- lock_vma_under_rcu() will be safe as the attempted read lock will bail;

Changes in the following files are not affecting NOMMU config:

task_mmu.c - not compiled when CONFIG_MMU=n;
pagewalk.c - not compiled when CONFIG_MMU=n;
userfaultfd.c - not compiled when CONFIG_MMU=n (CONFIG_USERFAULTFD depends
on CONFIG_MMU);

The following changes in the BPF code are made to keep NOMMU config
working like before:

stack_map_lock_vma() - keeps mmap_lock in NOMMU config;
bpf_iter_task_vma_new() - bails out in NOMMU config;

rust: cpufreq: reject NULL from cpufreq_cpu_get()

cpufreq_cpu_get() returns either a referenced policy or NULL.
PolicyCpu::from_cpu() passed its return value to from_err_ptr(), which
rejects ERR_PTR values but accepts NULL.

If the lookup fails, Policy::from_raw_mut() therefore constructs a mutable
reference from NULL. Dropping the resulting PolicyCpu then passes the
invalid pointer to cpufreq_cpu_put(), causing an oops in kobject_put().

Reject NULL with NonNull before constructing the Policy reference. Return
ENODEV instead.

A KUnit negative-control run reproduced the oops with the original
conversion. The same test passed with this change. The reproducer is
available on request.
